name: SH1107 1.12" 128×128 OLED display (I2C)
description: 1.12 inch monochrome 128×128 white OLED driven by a Sino Wealth SH1107 controller over I2C at address 0x3D (0x3C with the A0 jumper bridged or A0 tied to GND). The board has a 3.3 V regulator, a 12 V boost converter for the panel and level shifting, so it runs from 3–5 V. It also has SPI (close jumper J1); this part models the default I2C mode. Sold as: Adafruit Monochrome 1.12" 128x128 OLED Graphic Display (SH1107, STEMMA QT, product #5297), 8-pin header numbered as in Adafruit's Eagle board file (JP2 pad 1 = SDA): 1 Data (SDA), 2 Clk (SCL), 3 DC (A0), 4 Rst, 5 CS, 6 3Vo, 7 VIN, 8 GND; the silkscreen reads GND ... Data left to right, i.e. pin 8 to pin 1.
eli5: A small square black-and-white screen with 128 by 128 dots that your board can draw text and pictures on using just two wires.

pins.name: Data
pins.description: I2C data (SDA), BSS138 level-shifted; 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN on the board

pins.name: Clk
pins.description: I2C clock (SCL), BSS138 level-shifted; 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN on the board

pins.name: DC
pins.description: Printed DC / A0. In I2C mode this is the address select SA0: open (pulled high) = 0x3D, tied to GND = 0x3C. In SPI mode it is data/command. Leave unconnected for 0x3D

pins.name: Rst
pins.description: Display reset, active low (diode-isolated, 10 kOhm pull-up and APX803 power-on reset on the board); optional, leave unconnected for basic use

pins.name: CS
pins.description: SPI chip select (SPI mode only); diode-isolated with a 10 kOhm pull-up on the board, leave unconnected in I2C mode

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (about 100 mA spare); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3-5 V (reverse-polarity protected, on-board AP2112K 3.3 V regulator and 12 V boost). SDA/SCL are pulled up to VIN, so use 3.3 V with an ESP32, Pico or Raspberry Pi

buildNotes: Header pins 1-8 (Adafruit JP2 numbering): Data, Clk, DC/A0, Rst, CS, 3Vo, VIN, GND. On the silkscreen they read GND ... Data left to right, so pin 1 is the Data end. Always wire by the printed label. For I2C you only need GND, VIN, Clk (SCL) and Data (SDA), or just plug in a STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable.
I2C address is 0x3D out of the box (A0 open). Bridge the A0 jumper on the back or tie the DC/A0 pin to GND for 0x3C.
The board ships in I2C mode (J1 open). Do not bridge J1 unless you want SPI; the STEMMA QT ports only work in I2C mode.
SDA and SCL have 10 kOhm pull-ups to VIN: power the board from 3.3 V when it is wired to a 3.3 V board (ESP32, Pico, Raspberry Pi).
This is an SH1107, not an SSD1306 or SH1106: those drivers show garbage. Use sh1107.py, which sends each pixel row as one RAM column in vertical addressing mode.
The panel's 12 V comes from an on-board boost converter, so a fully lit screen can draw around 80 mA from VIN (typically about 35 mA). Power it from the 3V3 pin, not a GPIO.
The frame buffer is 2 KB; a full redraw over I2C at 400 kHz takes roughly 60-100 ms.
OLEDs burn in: blank the screen or call poweroff() when nothing needs to be shown for a long time.

driver.code:
# sh1107.py - MicroPython I2C driver for the 128x128 SH1107 OLED
# (Adafruit Monochrome 1.12" 128x128 OLED, product 5297).
#
# Follows the Sino Wealth SH1107 V2.1 datasheet and the panel maker's
# (ZJY-2828TSWIG01) power-up example:
#   control byte 0x00 = command bytes follow, 0x40 = display data follows;
#   AD 8A turns the internal DC-DC off (the board has its own 12 V boost);
#   display offset 0 for this board (Adafruit's driver value for #5297);
#   clear RAM, then AF (display on) and wait 100 ms.
#
# Memory: the SH1107 RAM is 16 pages x 128 columns. Each page byte drives
# 8 SEG lines; the column address drives a COM line. On this board the
# SEG lines run across the glass and COM lines down it, so this driver
# keeps a row-major MONO_HMSB frame buffer (16 bytes per pixel row, bit 0 =
# leftmost pixel) and sends each row y to column y in vertical addressing
# mode (21H), where the page address advances after every byte.
# Segment remap A1 + COM scan C0 with offset 0 is the upright setting that
# peter-l5's SH1107 driver (tested on this board) uses at rotate=0;
# rotate180() switches to A0 + C8.

from micropython import const
import framebuf
import time

_DISPLAY_OFF = const(0xAE)
_DISPLAY_ON = const(0xAF)
_SET_CONTRAST = const(0x81)
_SET_DCDC = const(0xAD)
_VERTICAL_ADDR = const(0x21)
_SEG_REMAP = const(0xA0)
_COM_SCAN = const(0xC0)
_START_LINE = const(0xDC)
_DISPLAY_OFFSET = const(0xD3)
_CLOCK_DIV = const(0xD5)
_PRECHARGE = const(0xD9)
_VCOM_DESELECT = const(0xDB)
_MULTIPLEX = const(0xA8)
_ENTIRE_ON_RESUME = const(0xA4)
_NORMAL_DISPLAY = const(0xA6)
_PAGE_ADDR = const(0xB0)


class SH1107_I2C(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    def __init__(self, width, height, i2c, addr=0x3D, res=None):
        if width != 128 or height != 128:
            raise ValueError('this driver is for the 128x128 panel')
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.res = res
        self.stride = width // 8
        self.buffer = bytearray(self.stride * height)
        self._mv = memoryview(self.buffer)
        self._row_cmd = bytearray(4)
        self._row_cmd[0] = 0x00
        self._flipped = False
        super().__init__(self.buffer, width, height, framebuf.MONO_HMSB)
        self.reset()
        self.init_display()

    def write_cmd(self, *cmds):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((0x00,) + cmds))

    def reset(self):
        # The board has an APX803 power-on reset; RST is only needed to
        # recover a display that got noise on its bus. Low pulse >= 10 us.
        if self.res is not None:
            self.res.init(self.res.OUT, value=1)
            time.sleep_ms(1)
            self.res(0)
            time.sleep_ms(1)
            self.res(1)
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    def init_display(self):
        self.write_cmd(_DISPLAY_OFF)
        self.write_cmd(_CLOCK_DIV, 0x51)
        self.write_cmd(_SET_CONTRAST, 0x4F)
        self.write_cmd(_SET_DCDC, 0x8A)        # internal DC-DC off
        self.write_cmd(_VERTICAL_ADDR)
        self.write_cmd(_START_LINE, 0x00)
        self.write_cmd(_DISPLAY_OFFSET, 0x00)
        self.write_cmd(_PRECHARGE, 0x22)
        self.write_cmd(_VCOM_DESELECT, 0x35)
        self.write_cmd(_MULTIPLEX, 0x7F)       # 128 COM lines
        self.write_cmd(_ENTIRE_ON_RESUME)
        self.write_cmd(_NORMAL_DISPLAY)
        self.rotate180(False, update=False)
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()                            # clear RAM before turning on
        self.poweron()

    def poweron(self):
        self.write_cmd(_DISPLAY_ON)
        time.sleep_ms(100)                     # datasheet: wait 100 ms

    def poweroff(self):
        self.write_cmd(_DISPLAY_OFF)

    def contrast(self, value):
        self.write_cmd(_SET_CONTRAST, value & 0xFF)

    def invert(self, on):
        self.write_cmd(_NORMAL_DISPLAY | (1 if on else 0))

    def rotate180(self, on=True, update=True):
        # A1/C0 = upright on this board, A0/C8 = turned 180 degrees.
        self._flipped = bool(on)
        self.write_cmd(_SEG_REMAP | (0 if on else 1))
        self.write_cmd(_COM_SCAN | (0x08 if on else 0x00))
        if update:
            self.show()

    def show(self):
        cmd = self._row_cmd
        mv = self._mv
        stride = self.stride
        for y in range(self.height):
            cmd[1] = _PAGE_ADDR                # page 0
            cmd[2] = y & 0x0F                  # column low nibble
            cmd[3] = 0x10 | (y >> 4)           # column high bits
            self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, cmd)
            start = y * stride
            self.i2c.writevto(self.addr, (b'\x40', mv[start:start + stride]))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sh1107 import SH1107_I2C

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=400000)
oled = SH1107_I2C(128, 128, i2c, addr=0x3D)
oled.fill(0)
oled.text('SH1107 OLED', 0, 0)
oled.text('128x128 I2C', 0, 60)
oled.text('Bottom row', 0, 120)
oled.show()
print('drawn')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
